h: Bakole Steps In For Injured Opetaia To Face Wilder
sum: The Cardiff co-main event has a new look less than three weeks out, and Wilder’s night just got a lot heavier.
body: Jai Opetaia is out of his heavyweight debut against Deontay Wilder after aggravating a hand injury in camp. Martin Bakole (22-2-1, 16 KOs) takes his place in the co-main event of Fury vs Joshua on December 11, and the swap was made official on Monday.
It changes the fight completely. Instead of a smaller, faster cruiserweight, Wilder now faces a genuine heavyweight with real power.

Bakole’s last short-notice call did not go well. He came in out of shape against Joseph Parker and was stopped in the second round, then needed a fortunate draw against Efe Ajagba. He hasn’t fought in about 18 months.
Why it matters: Wilder has looked like a fading force since his trilogy with Fury ended in 2021. A win keeps him relevant at heavyweight. A loss to a rusty Bakole could end the conversation.

h: Fury Promises Joshua Won’t Hear The Final Bell
sum: At the launch press conference, Fury said he’s done boxing clever. He’s coming to knock Joshua out.
q: I’m gonna catch him, and when I do, it’s gonna be curtains.
ctx: Fury vs Joshua launch press conference
body: Tyson Fury didn’t wait for fight week to make his prediction. At the London launch press conference for their December 11 fight in Cardiff, he laid out the whole plan: a fast start, no running, no boxing, just a straight fight he compared to the gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

Joshua didn’t flinch. He said Fury’s knockout talk is exactly the energy he wants, and it’s what will push him through the extra rounds in the gym. When Fury joked that Joshua was built like a marble statue but couldn’t take a shot, Joshua laughed it off: “That’s also true.”
Why it matters: Fury is 38 and Joshua turns 37 before fight night. After a decade of failed talks, this is the fight both men will be remembered for.

h: Lopes Moves Up And Asks Oliveira For A War
sum: His first fight at 155 is for the BMF belt, and he has zero interest in playing it safe.
q: I want to get in there and throw down. Let’s see who goes down first.
ctx: On his UFC 335 BMF title fight
body: Diego Lopes is skipping the warm-up. The two-time featherweight title challenger makes his lightweight debut in the UFC 335 main event against Charles Oliveira on December 12, with the BMF belt on the line.

He says he respects Oliveira, but believes his all-action style is what the BMF title is supposed to be about. He wants to stand in the pocket with one of the most dangerous finishers the UFC has ever had.
Dana White is already bracing for it, calling the matchup “absolutely bat s*** crazy.”
Why it matters: Oliveira and Lopes have 56 professional finishes between them. Neither man knows how to have a boring fight.

h: Benavidez Says Cieślak Is The Last Step Before Something Bigger
sum: The unbeaten champion comes home to Arizona with three belts on the line and his eyes on a much bigger name.
q: I’m the best fighter in all of boxing, but I have to prove it.
ctx: Benavidez vs Cieślak kickoff press conference
body: David Benavidez insists he isn’t looking past Michał Cieślak. Thirteen weeks into camp, he says his focus is fully on the Polish WBC champion, who he meets on December 5 in Glendale, Arizona.
He called his last fight probably the best performance of his career, and says beating Cieślak would make him the king of the cruiserweight division.
Cieślak isn’t intimidated. He watched Benavidez beat Zurdo Ramírez, thought he fought pretty well, and says December 5 will show Benavidez what he should have done better.
Why it matters: Benavidez calls this the last thing standing in the way of an even bigger fight, and he’s been open in recent interviews about wanting Oleksandr Usyk next.

h: Joshua Isn’t Buying Fury’s Nice-Guy Act
sum: Fury praised AJ and offered him a post-fight pint. Joshua smiled and kept his guard up.
q: I don’t know if I can trust you.
ctx: Replying to Fury’s post-fight Guinness invite
body: The launch press conference was friendlier than anyone expected. Fury called Joshua a role model for British boxing, said he even defends him to fans he meets in the street, and suggested they go for a pint of Guinness once the fighting is done.
Joshua wasn’t biting. Fury has played mind games before big fights for years, and AJ answered the invite with a smile and a warning.
The face-off ended with Joshua tickling Fury in the stomach, the strangest moment of a strange afternoon.
Why it matters: A friendly Fury can be the most dangerous Fury. Joshua is making it clear he won’t be talked into relaxing.

h: Oliveira Says He’s Next In Line For The Lightweight Title
sum: The BMF champion has a plan for 2027, and it starts with getting through Lopes.
q: If he retires, then it’s me and Arman fighting for the vacant title.
body: Charles Oliveira took the BMF belt from Max Holloway at UFC 326. Now he defends it against Diego Lopes, but the belt he really wants is the one he used to hold.
Asked whether winning the UFC lightweight title again before he retires still matters to him, Oliveira kept it short: “That’s my dream.”
He says everyone knows he’s a problem for the division and that he’s next. First, he wants the UFC to find out what Justin Gaethje plans to do.
Why it matters: If Gaethje steps away, Oliveira sees a vacant-title fight with Arman Tsarukyan. A loss to Lopes would wipe that plan out.

h: Cieślak Plans To Take All Three Belts Back To Poland
sum: The away fighter in Glendale isn’t treating this as a trip to lose.
q: I will bring all three belts back to Poland after December 5.
body: Michał Cieślak holds the WBC cruiserweight title and walks into Benavidez’s home crowd in Glendale, Arizona, on December 5. The WBA and WBO belts are on the line too.
He doesn’t sound worried about the crowd or the favorite. Cieślak has studied Benavidez’s recent work and believes he can expose what Benavidez didn’t do well.
Why it matters: Most expect a Benavidez win. An upset would blow up the cruiserweight division and every big plan Benavidez has for 2027.

h: Joshua On Fury Fight: ‘No Better Time Than Now’
sum: After years of failed talks, AJ sounds like a man who’s just glad it’s finally real.
q: It had to happen at some stage and there’s no better time than now.
ctx: Fury vs Joshua launch press conference
body: Fury and Joshua first shared a ring in a 2010 sparring session, when Fury was an up-and-coming pro and Joshua was still an amateur. Fans have wanted the real thing for most of the years since.
Joshua says he knows people have argued about this fight in pubs, and that family members have fallen out over who wins. He says he’s just happy to be fighting and fulfilling his destiny.
Why it matters: For years the fight felt like it would never happen. Now both men are talking like it’s the last big chapter of their careers.
